subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — notice smoothing and TfC staircase proposal
messages:
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@kestrelpay.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@kestrelpay.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines (term/renewal/termination)

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal team attached a redline of the MSA and the order form focusing on term and termination mechanics. High level: we want a longer notice window for cancellations (60 days), no termination-for-convenience during the initial 12-month committed term, and a clear auto-renew cadence (12 months) thereafter.

Key items in the redline (attached):
- Initial term: 12 months, no TfC during initial term
- Auto-renew: 12-month renewals unless Customer gives 60-day notice before renewal
- Data/transition obligations triggered on termination (30-day handover window)

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the 60-day opt-out window and the restriction on TfC for the initial term. Procurement would like a proposed final by the first week of September.

Attachments: Kestrel_Redlines_20260825.pdf (redlined MSA + order form)

Best,
Susan Lee
General Counsel, Kestrel Payments

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@kestrelpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (term/renewal/termination)

Susan —

Appreciate the clear redlines and the timeline. We can prioritize this. I want to propose a compromise that balances Kestrel's need for predictability and Redwood's need for commercial flexibility. Proposed counterpoints below (we'll follow up with a tracked Word doc):

1) Initial term: keep 12 months. We can agree to remove unilateral TfC by Customer during the initial term, contingent on an agreed escrow/transition fee schedule to cover potential uplift costs.

2) Auto-renew: agree on 12-month renewals, but Redwood requests a 90-day opt-out notice before renewal rather than 60 days. Rationale: our operational lead time for capacity and reserved pools is typically 60–75 days.

3) TfC after initial term: allow mutual termination for convenience (either party) after the initial 12 months with a staged notice ‘staircase’ depending on remaining committed term:
   - Months 13–18: 120 days notice + 1 month service credit
   - Months 19–30: 90 days notice + pro rata refund of unused prepaid months
   - After month 30: 60 days notice

4) Transition: clarify data export SLA (30 days) and offer an extended support window (30 additional days of hands-on migration) as an option in the order form.

Action items:
- Aditya, can the legal team draft counters in track changes (I'll attach a baseline doc)?
- Rishi, can you confirm the commercial fallback (service credit vs escrow) for sales ops?

I'll attach a one-page term summary to send back to Kestrel.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Stephanie / team —

Thanks for the summary. I reviewed Kestrel's redlines and Stephanie's suggested staircase. Legal is generally comfortable with a staircase approach as a compromise, provided we: (a) include discrete service-credit language tied to remaining committed spend, and (b) preserve Redwood's right to delay opt-outs on dedicated capacity with matching credit. Proposed concrete text (to be added to counter redline):

- Auto-Renewal: "Unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current Term, the Term shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods."
- Termination for Convenience (post-initial term): include a table (we'll attach) that maps remaining committed months to notice and remedy (service credit or escrow). Example: Months 13–18: 120 days notice, service credit = 15% of trailing 3-month ARR; Months 19–30: 90 days notice, pro rata; After 30 months: 60 days notice.
- Initial Term carve: "Customer shall not terminate for convenience during the Initial Term unless Customer pays an early termination fee equal to the remainder of the Initial Term fees, less reasonable mitigation credits."

Attachments I will push in the counter: Redwood_Term_Counter_20260825.docx (tracked changes), Term_Summary_TABLE.csv.

Stephanie: once you confirm the service-credit approach (credit % vs escrow), I'll finalize redline and send to Susan. Rishi: flag any commercial constraints on refunds/credits for Dedicated customers — we need that input to finalize wording.

Aditya
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference
